      - text: Lesson 6.1 · Mechanism
    - heading "Two hormones, two layers of skin." [level=2]
    - paragraph: Growth hormone acts mostly in the dermis. Its receptor is expressed more by fibroblasts than by keratinocytes, and it increases fibroblast numbers and supports collagen synthesis. IGF-1, made locally by fibroblasts and melanocytes, reaches keratinocytes through the IGF-1 receptor and makes them divide. Human hair follicles even run their own small growth-hormone loop in the laboratory. With age, GH secretion and IGF-1 fall steadily; this is the somatopause.
